text.dek: 79 researched website-builder capabilities: 65 from Framer and Webflow, 14 more from Adobe Express and Canva. FormWeb is graded on executed local acceptance; the four others are graded from their official documentation, fetched on 10 and 11 October 2026, so their scores are lower bounds rather than proof of absence.
text.baseline: 65 targets from Framer and Webflow (v0.1.0) plus 14 from Adobe Express and Canva (v0.3.0)
text.changes: v0.5.3 closes one row: background removal and image cleanup (None to Full), handed to formvis. The score moves from 73.0 to 74.0 of 79.
text.history: Scores are recomputed from each release's recorded per-row grades. The jump in rows at v0.3.0 is the wider baseline, not a regression.
text.parity: Full means implemented and accepted end to end in FormWeb, or documented natively by a vendor. Partial means narrower than the target, or reached only through an integration. None means not built (FormWeb) or not found in the sources read (vendors); the status word says which: Not found, Not offered or Retired.
method: Each grade comes from executed commands, SDK and MCP calls, editor flows and compiled browser output retained with the release; a stored value without a consuming workflow does not earn Full.
Each cell rests on the cited official page. Unknown is not absence: a None marked Not found means only that the sources read did not show it.
Full counts 1, Partial one half, None 0, over all rows. Documented counts as Full and Integration as Partial for the vendors.

Per-row grades for every release are kept in docs/comparisons/data/formweb-parity.json; ./formweb comparisons build renders this page and the change tables from them, and ./formweb comparisons embed puts it in the FormAI matrix.
